title: diagnose/adopt mode detection + both READMEs
next_action: ROUND 1 FINDING FIXED 2026-08-18, awaiting a fresh V4. The finding: len(tracks)==1 was a proxy for 'no register exists' and is ALSO true when the register declares exactly one track — so every board row, every commitment row and every project-wide file was scored as that track's, ignoring the Track column the scanner already reads and the schema's rule that a blank Track means the implicit main track. A project declaring one pipeline track with its ordinary work in untracked rows scored project 7 / pipeline 4 and got a MODE-01 warn TELLING THE USER TO CHANGE A MODE CELL THAT WAS CORRECT. All four sites addressed: the proxy now asks the declaredness question that was already being computed sixty lines below for the payload; the implicit main track is enumerated when untracked rows put one on the board; and file evidence is split into two buckets because lumping them was the bug in BOTH directions — Intake, answer files and SRC digests are evidence of a WORK SHAPE and reach any track that might have it, while phase/ and OKR objectives describe the REPOSITORY and reach only the project-wide track. TWO WRONG FIXES FIRST, both caught by existing tests that were right: withholding shape evidence made a declared queue track unreadable; and a fourth test asserts deliberately that ONE declared track does get the project-wide signals, which contradicts the finding until you read its board — it has NO ROWS. The finding's scenario is one declared track AND untracked rows beside it. So the rule is not how many tracks are declared, it is whether there is a project-wide track to own them. ALSO CORRECTED: the row previously claimed 8 and 10 mode mentions in the two READMEs; the reviewer measured 8 and 8 and I had written a number without running it.

next_action: V4 ROUND 3: FAIL on guarantee 3, ADR-004 STANDS — fixed 2026-08-18. The reviewer stopped guessing where the third crash was and ENUMERATED ALL FIVE PLACES MIGRATION WRITES TO A PROJECT. THE AXIS ALL THREE ROUNDS MISSED: a read-only DIRECTORY, not a read-only file — write_atomic renames, and a rename needs write permission on the directory, which is why every existing test, all driving read-only through a file, passed throughout. FIXED all three plus the scratch write in Linter.errors, guarded rather than exempted because an exemption list is where this kind of guard rots. AND THE ENUMERATION IS NOW A STANDING CHECK: tests/test_migrate.py TestEveryWriteSiteIsGuarded walks the AST and fails if any write call sits outside a try — proved by planting a sixth site after the guard was written and watching it go red. That is the fix; the three patches are not. Guarantees 1, 2, 4, 5 all PASS on gimegime-pmo (365 to 380 ids, none lost, 59 to 15, 30 declared, PolyForge refused in one sentence). next_action: FOUND 2026-08-18 while fixing TASK-044's planning crash, by asserting what I ASSUMED rather than what happens — the test failed and the code was right. write_atomic writes a .tmp and calls Path.replace, and A RENAME NEEDS WRITE PERMISSION ON THE DIRECTORY, NOT ON THE TARGET. So a file the user has chmod-ed read-only is migrated like any other, and nothing in the plan says the bit was there. THE QUESTION IS A POLICY ONE ABOUT SOMEBODY ELSE'S FILES and I deliberately did not decide it mid-fix: (a) the bit is an explicit user signal and ADR-004's whole posture is 'the user declares', so migration should refuse or at least name it; (b) it may be incidental — copied off a read-only medium, or a stale mode from an archive — and refusing would block a migration for a reason unrelated to shape. PINNED BY A TEST TODAY: the file IS migrated, and the restore point carries its original bytes, so the recovery path covers it — which is what makes the current behaviour survivable rather than merely undetected. NOT TRUE TODAY: that the plan mentions the mode at all. Whichever way this is decided, TASK-044-spec says migration is 'not silent — every file it touched, listed, with what changed in each', and a permission it overrode belongs in that list.
